div.span: - Target tracking creates them for you. AlarmHigh needs 3 datapoints above the target, AlarmLow needs 15 below it. That asymmetry is deliberate: grow fast, shrink carefully.

div.b: The service gets a new desiredCount

div.span: - ECS starts or stops tasks to match, the ALB registers them, and the next minute of metrics already reflects the change. The loop has closed.

div.b: Two traps this lab walks into

div.div: - The ceiling is real. With ten tasks at 100 % CPU the alarm stays in ALARM but the count never passes max_capacity. Raise the ceiling or give each task more CPU.

- Measure before you pick a target. A single-threaded app on 0.25 vCPU alternates between 0 and 100 %, so its average plateau sits near 50 %. With a 50 % target the alarm never fires, which is why this lab uses 30 %.
